title: Run tonight's new Swift tests for real

proofs.run: sh scripts/swift-test-here.sh (the whole package target) on a tree whose library matches; quote the run's summary line and, from the log, the line `Test <name> passed` of each of the eight tests of proof 0
proofs.pass: all eight names appear as passed; the summary line `Test run with N tests ... passed` is quoted with the eight lines

notes: The five items of the acceptance and their tests: MessageBodySamplesTests (Tests/Unit/MessageBodySamplesTests.swift:13 everySampleMailIsServedAndNotEmpty, :23 theSamplesKeepTheirHtmlAndTheirFigures); AttachmentSetBlockedTests (Tests/Unit/AttachmentSetBlockedTests.swift:9 aBlockedRemotePictureIsNotAFile, :16 aRealInlinePictureStaysListedBesideABlockedOne, :22 theBlockedPlaceholderIsTheCoresOwn); the two Cmd-J tests in ShortcutsTests (Tests/Unit/ShortcutsTests.swift:74 everyKeyOfTheV8ListIsBoundInTheSuperhumanPreset and :91 theSuperhumanPresetBindsNothingElseButTheDeclaredExtras; the latter lists the Cmd-J key among the declared extras at :94 and expects it bound to ai-reply at :98, which the old log's red lines contradicted before that edit); the WindowBridge no-app test (Tests/Unit/WindowBridgeNoAppTests.swift:13 windowFactsAreEmptyWhenThereIsNoApplication; its mutant note at lines 10-11, reading NSApp.windows directly, is not given as a find string because the break spans several lines). The mutant here removes the blocked-picture filter (Sources/Features/AttachmentsMac/AttachmentSet.swift:57). Whether the Cmd-J tests are green now is not known: the reader's log (unit-final.log:851-884) may be older than the edit that added the key to the extras; proof 1 settles it. If ShortcutsTests is red on the current HEAD, the item stays open with the named test.
